subject: Unexpected mid-month spike and payment hold — token trace request
messages:
From: Aditi Suresh <aditi@parcellytics.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-12T09:34:12Z
Subject: Unexpected mid-month spike and payment hold

Hi Connor,

We put this on your radar — Parcellytics has a large unexpected usage spike on Oct 1–10 that pushed us over our committed band and triggered a collection hold from our AP team. Attached is the invoice we received (invoice_20271001.pdf).

We do not recognize the pattern: the requests look like normal production traffic but the token counts per request are ~2x what we expect. Could you provide token-level evidence (request IDs + per-request token counts and timestamps) for the period 2027-10-01 through 2027-10-10?

Also: we need the VAT split by legal entity. Parcellytics runs two EU entities (BV and GmbH) and the invoice was issued to the wrong entity — our tax team will not release payment until we get a corrected VAT breakdown.

AP has placed a temporary hold on the payment until we reconcile. We appreciate a quick turnaround — this is flagged as high priority internally.

Thanks,
Aditi Suresh
Head of Finance | Parcellytics
ap-team@parcellytics.com

Attachments: invoice_20271001.pdf
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Aditi Suresh <aditi@parcellytics.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-12T14:05:03Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike and payment hold

Aditi — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We’ll investigate immediately.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I’ve looped in our billing and metering team (Hannah and Ben).
- Hannah will pull token-level traces and a sample CSV for the window you specified.
- Ben will run a quick audit to see if any new routing/aux model variants could have doubled tokenization counts.
- We can offer a provisional credit while we complete the trace if there’s evidence of mis-attribution.

Two quick asks to speed things up:
1) Please confirm which Parcellytics legal entity should be listed on a corrected invoice (BV vs GmbH) and the PO number to match.
2) If you have 3–5 example request IDs or timestamps that look anomalous on your side, please forward them — that will reduce investigation time.

I’ll update you within 24 business hours with an initial sample.

—Connor O’Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, Aditi Suresh <aditi@parcellytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-13T08:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike and payment hold

Hi Aditi / Connor —

We started the token-trace pull for 2027-10-01 → 2027-10-10. To produce an actionable CSV, I need either:
- 3 sample request IDs (request_id) + timestamps (UTC), OR
- a short time-range (e.g., 2027-10-04T14:00 → 2027-10-04T15:00) and we’ll return all requests in that window.

What I will provide: a CSV with columns (request_id, timestamp_utc, model, tokens_input, tokens_output, token_total, route_variant).

I’m attaching a small sample template (usage-sample-queries.csv) — please populate with any request_ids you can. If you prefer, we can run the full account-wide scan and redact PII, but that will take ~48 hours.

On VAT: we can issue a corrected invoice and split the VAT across the entity you confirm. We’ll need the destination entity’s VAT reg number and the PO to reissue the credit memo correctly.

Finally, for provisional credit: we can hold 15% of the disputed amount pending the full audit. We’ll prepare a credit memo and a short acknowledgement form (DocuSign) — please confirm who in Parcellytics is authorized to sign.

Attachments: usage-sample-queries.csv

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Billing & Metering | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
From: Aditi Suresh <aditi@parcellytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-13T10:22:10Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike and payment hold

Thanks, Hannah.

We attached a short list of 4 request IDs that our AP and engineering teams flagged (see PO and supporting doc attached if you need the internal ticket id). The correct billing entity should be Parcellytics BV — VAT reg NL123456789. PO# PL-2027-Q4-009.

Example request ids/timestamps:
- req_8d9b3f9e — 2027-10-04T14:05:32Z
- req_8d9b4512 — 2027-10-04T14:05:38Z
- req_8d9b77a1 — 2027-10-06T09:12:04Z
- req_8d9c001f — 2027-10-07T21:44:09Z

Per our AP team: payment will remain on hold until we receive either (a) evidence that the counts are correct, or (b) a corrected invoice + credit memo we can attach to the payment release. We can sign the DocuSign acknowledgement — authorized signer is Aditi Suresh (Head of Finance).

I’m attaching PO and the internal AP hold notice (po_parcellytics_2027Q4.pdf). Please let me know ETA on the CSV and whether you’ll propose a provisional credit.

Best,
Aditi
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Aditi Suresh <aditi@parcellytics.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-14T16:45:33Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike and payment hold

Hi Aditi —

Thanks for the request IDs and PO. We completed the preliminary trace and attached a sanitized token-trace-log.txt with per-request token totals for the four IDs you provided plus surrounding requests in the same minute. Summary findings:
- The four flagged requests show token_total values 1.9–2.1x higher than the median for the same endpoint.
- We identified an aux-routing experiment (route_variant: aux-v2-preview) that was enabled for a small subset of traffic during Oct 2–6; aux-v2 applies a longer system prompt which explains the higher tokens.
- There is no evidence of double-billing in our ledger; the meter recorded the longer prompt as token consumption.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) We can reissue the invoice to Parcellytics BV (VAT NL123456789) and produce a credit memo for 15% of the disputed amount as provisional relief while you review the full audit.
2) We’ll run a full account trace for Oct 1–10 and provide a complete CSV within 48 business hours (redacted as needed).
3) To lift the AP hold we need the signed DocuSign acknowledgement we’ll generate; once signed we’ll post the credit memo and reissue the corrected invoice.

I’ve attached token-trace-log.txt (sanitized). If you’d like us to filter the audit to only production project IDs, confirm the project IDs and we’ll narrow the export.

—Ben Carter
Sr. Billing Analyst | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: token-trace-log.txt
